hits.name: @levelsio
hits.text:
I opened the box form @DHH and it's the Dell XPS 14 with @omarchy loaded on it!

Set up was very easy, fast and flawless, I think it took less than a minute on first opening it

Omarchy asks you lots of questions to set it up for you, kind of like an onboarding, but not in an annoying way like Windows would do these days with too many useless questions, every question here makes sense

It sets up your Git and your AI agent of choice like Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode

Everything worked flawlessly with no bugs at all, really smooth

Then you're inside, and you see the famous Omarchy wallpaper, and then it gets a bit hard (for me at least) because I had to figure out the shortcuts

Luckily @jankeesvw helped me figure them out but I'm still learning

I'll be setting up my SSH to my VPS servers so I can work from there. And also I'd like to see if I can use Claude Code to customize Omarchy to my own liking, like generating my own apps etc.

I'll report back!

Part 2 of the video is in the reply (after I fixed the power)
hits.hook: I opened the box form @DHH and it's the Dell XPS 14 with @omarchy loaded on it!  Set up was very easy, fast and flawless
hits.draft_en:
DHH sent Pieter a Dell XPS 14 running Omarchy. His take: setup took under a minute, and the onboarding asks only questions that matter, including which coding agent to install (Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode). 169k views.

That's the new bar for dev machines: the agent is part of first boot, like Git.

If you ship a dev tool, ask yourself whether it would make the cut in a one-minute setup. If not, it needs a CLI or an MCP endpoint an agent can install.
hits.video_tip: 12s: laptop first boot, a setup wizard asking 'pick your coding agent', terminal ready in under a minute, caption agent on first boot.

outsiders.name: Artificial Analysis
outsiders.text:
Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index

Gemini 4 Carbon scores 59 on Intelligence Index v5, driven by leading performance in complex reasoning, knowledge, and scientific tasks. It also has large gains in coding and knowledge work, particularly when compared to other Gemini models, but it is not leading in all these areas.

As with launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Gemini 4 Carbon is being rolled out to selected users and is not yet publicly available. Google is offering a 50% launch discount, with no confirmed end date. All our charts and figures use standard pricing for both Gemini 4 Carbon and Argon.

Key results for Gemini 4 Carbon with high reasoning:
➤ Gemini 4 Carbon leads the Intelligence Index v5, with the #1 score in 4 of the 9 Index evaluations: HLE-Diamond, Terminal-Bench-Science, AA-Omniscience, AutomationBench-AA. Carbon makes substantial gains elsewhere but is not leading in coding and knowledge work

➤ Behind only Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents: With Antigravity CLI, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 59 only 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 62) on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Carbon ranks second on both Terminal-Bench 4.0 (64%) and FrontierCode v1.1 (51%), behind Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 56%. Google has historically underperformed in this area and so this improvement stands out

➤ Improved agentic knowledge work, but not yet leading: On AA-Briefcase, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 1609 Elo, a 126-point improvement over Gemini 4 Argon (high, 1483), but still behind models including Grok 4.7 (xhigh, 1638), Muse Wonder (max, 1659) and Kimi K3.1 Pro (1678). The largest gain comes from Presentation, up 293 Elo to 1598, alongside a 120-point improvement in Analytical Quality to 1671

➤ Lower Cost per Task than Claude Opus 5.5 for comparable overall intelligence: Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04) but ~1.2x GPT-6 Astra (max, $6.25). It uses 123k output tokens per task, 29% fewer than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 173k). At the same $4/$20 standard pricing, its Cost per Task is in line with Gemini 4 Argon ($7.68), while scoring 9 points higher on the Intelligence Index

➤ Leading AA-Omniscience v1.1 score, with low hallucination: Gemini 4 Carbon scores 54 on our recently updated AA-Omniscience v1.1, 6 points ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 48) and 8 points ahead of Gemini 4 Argon (46). Accuracy (% correct) rises 10 points over Argon to 58%, while its hallucination rate rises from 4% to 11%. This is still the second lowest of any model, behind only Argon, compared with 50% for both Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max)

Key model details:
➤ Context Window: 1M tokens
➤ Multimodality: Text, image, video, and speech input, with text output
➤ Pricing: $4/$20 per 1M input/output tokens, the same as Gemini 4 Argon’s standard pricing, with a 50% discount. Cached input tokens receive a 95% discount ($0.20 per 1M)

Congratulations to the @GoogleDeepMind team!
outsiders.hook: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is the new #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5, and second only to Claude Opus
outsiders.note: Benchmark org's ranking; quoted by @swyx. Check on your own tasks

virals.angle: Every app needs an agent door
virals.draft_en:
Pieter Levels made two sites agent-usable in one day. His travel site went into the MCP directories (he had to add OAuth, since they don't take bare API keys), and his hotel site now lets an agent find, book and review hotels.

His rule: apps should be MCP and API accessible at feature parity with the website.

Shopify is doing the big-company version, opening Shop Pay as a checkout inside agents.

List the three things users do most on your product. If an agent can't do them, that's your roadmap.
virals.inspired_by: @levelsio MCP directories (40k, 182 bookmarks) + hotel site MCP (15k) + Shopify Shop Pay for agents (outsider)
virals.video_tip: 12s: website on the left, agent chat on the right doing the same three actions, caption feature parity for agents.

virals.draft_en:
Google shipped Gemini 4 Carbon two weeks after Argon, and Artificial Analysis now ranks it #1 on their Intelligence Index v5 (second to Claude Opus 5.5 on coding agents). Mistral open-sourced a new Le Chonk the next day.

swyx's take: comeback season, with roughly twice the frontier labs we had a year ago.

The practical move isn't picking a winner. Keep the model behind one config line and a small eval of your own hardest tasks. Rerun it on every launch.
virals.inspired_by: @OfficialLoganK Gemini 4 Carbon (1.14M) + @ArtificialAnlys #1 on AAv5 (565k) + @swyx comeback season (15k) + @MistralAI Le Chonk (163k)
virals.video_tip: 10s: leaderboard reshuffling, then a tiny eval script rerunning and picking a model per task, caption your eval, not theirs.

virals.draft_en:
Alex Finn's walkthrough of five Grok Bot dashboards got 229k views and 4.1k bookmarks. One of them cut his usage.

People save setups they can copy.

The one dashboard worth building first: what your agent did today and what it cost. Most waste, like routines firing too often or runs that loop, shows up there within a week.
virals.inspired_by: @AlexFinn Grok Bot pages and dashboards (229k, 4.1k bookmarks) + @dharmesh agents running overnight (14k)
virals.video_tip: 12s: a dashboard with 'today' and 'usage' panels, one noisy routine highlighted and paused, caption see what your agent spends.

virals.draft_en:
Pieter Levels wants a zero tolerance rule for AI replies on X: one strike and you're out. 86k views, 604 replies.

You don't have to agree with the rule to see the cost. A generated reply is obvious in one line and makes people trust you less.

Use AI for the work before you post (research, outlines, checking claims). Keep the voice in replies yours, or skip the reply.
virals.inspired_by: @levelsio zero tolerance for AI replies (86k, 604 replies)
virals.video_tip: 8s: generic AI reply typed out, then deleted and replaced with one specific human sentence, caption your voice or nothing.

virals.draft_en:
Greg Isenberg compared building on OpenAI, Anthropic, Google or Grok models to ordering a McDonald's Diet Coke: the same crisp thing for everyone.

Meanwhile OpenAI is handing eligible Pro and Business users up to $500 a month in API credits to build apps and agents. More people, same models.

So the edge is what you add: your data, your distribution, a workflow nobody else has. Write those three down before you write code.
virals.inspired_by: @gregisenberg McDonald's Diet Coke (31k, 113 replies) + @OpenAIDevs $500/month API credits (1.66M)
virals.video_tip: 8s: four identical drinks with model logos, then hands adding a custom label to one, caption the model isn't the moat.

Off-lane watchlist posts are kept as hits but flagged skip in drafts.
